title: The Marsh That Came Back
paras: When green shoots appeared behind Bellwater Bay's broken sea wall, some residents called it a [[miracle|miracle]]. For decades, the ground had been dry and almost bare. A few [[superstitious|superstitious]] fishers linked its recovery to a lucky stone uncovered by the waves. Yet coastal scientist Amara Sen suspected a simpler explanation: seawater was returning to an ancient marsh.

The opening had appeared during a [[severe|severe]] winter storm, causing [[panic|panic]] among families whose gardens bordered the shore. Builders proposed sealing it with blocks joined using [[cement|cement]]. Sen suggested waiting. Salt marshes have an important [[function|function]]: their dense stems slow waves, while their roots hold muddy ground together. Repairing the wall immediately might prevent this natural protection from developing.

With permission from landowners, Sen helped [[establish|establish]] a monitoring programme. Her team used three [[criteria|criteria]] to judge recovery: plant cover, soil height and the number of young fish entering tidal pools. Monthly meetings allowed researchers to [[interact|interact]] with residents, who contributed photographs taken from their windows. These images revealed where water remained longest after each tide, helping the team choose suitable planting sites.

After two growing seasons, vegetation covered much of the sheltered ground, although exposed corners remained bare. The findings reached a committee in the national [[congress|congress]], which was reviewing coastal protection law. For Bellwater's residents, however, the most persuasive evidence was closer: small fish now sheltered among stems where only cracked earth had been.
zh: 当贝尔沃特湾破损海堤后方冒出绿芽时，一些居民称之为奇迹。几十年来，那片土地一直干燥，几乎寸草不生。几位迷信的渔民认为，这次复苏与海浪冲出的一块幸运石有关。然而，海岸科学家阿玛拉·森猜测，原因其实更简单：海水正在重新流入一片古老的盐沼。
海堤上的缺口是在一场猛烈的冬季风暴中出现的，引发了花园紧邻海岸的那些家庭的恐慌。建筑工人提议用水泥黏合砌块，堵住缺口。森建议再等等。盐沼有一个重要作用：密集的植物茎秆可以减缓海浪，而根系则能固定泥泞的地面。立即修复海堤，可能会阻碍这种天然防护的形成。
获得土地所有者的许可后，森协助建立了一项监测计划。她的团队采用三项标准评估恢复情况：植被覆盖程度、土壤高度，以及进入潮汐水塘的幼鱼数量。每月的会议让研究人员能够与居民交流，居民还提供了从自家窗户拍摄的照片。这些照片显示了每次潮汐过后哪些地方积水时间最长，帮助团队选择合适的种植地点。
两个生长季过后，植被覆盖了大部分有遮蔽的地面，不过迎风浪的角落仍然光秃秃的。研究结果送到了国家议会的一个委员会，该委员会当时正在审议海岸保护法。不过，对贝尔沃特的居民来说，最有说服力的证据就在身边：过去只有龟裂泥土的地方，如今已有小鱼在植物茎秆间栖身。

q.s: One of the fishers was the first person to find the lucky stone.
q.why: 文中未说明谁最先发现幸运石。

q.s: Sen suggested delaying repairs to the sea wall.
q.why: 工人提议封堵缺口，森建议再等等。

q.s: Vegetation covered all the exposed corners after two growing seasons.
q.why: 两个生长季后，迎风浪的角落仍然光秃。
